title: New bent-toed gecko species found in Assam's Dima Hasao hills
summary: Cyrtodactylus dimensis was identified around Umrangso through field surveys and DNA analysis.
image_credit: Representative photo: a bent-toed gecko. Photo: Rohit Naniwadekar / [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lizard_Bent-toed_Gecko_Cyrtodactylus_IMG_7741_04.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0
body:
Researchers have described a new gecko species from the Umrangso area of Assam's Dima Hasao district. They named it Cyrtodactylus dimensis, and it belongs to the bent-toed gecko group.

The finding was published in the Journal of Threatened Taxa. The team included researchers from Mizoram University and other institutions, and they confirmed the species by combining a study of its body features with genetic analysis.

Field surveys took place in August 2025 and July 2026, with the geckos recorded in rocky micro-habitats around Umrangso.

The study was carried out by Krijoboti Thaosen, Mathipi Vabeiryureilai, Mara Duasa Hlychho and Hmar Tlawmte Lalremsanga. Their fieldwork added up to seven nights in total. The study was supported by the Union Ministry of Tribal Affairs and the Department of Science and Technology.

The researchers set the new gecko apart by the pattern of its scales and some special structures on its body. A statistical comparison of body measurements also showed it was different from the other geckos in the Cyrtodactylus khasiensis species group.

It is closely related to Cyrtodactylus vanarakshaka, another bent-toed gecko found in Dima Hasao. That species was described in September 2025 from the forested slopes of Jatinga in the Barail Hills, in a study published in the Journal of Asia-Pacific Biodiversity. Its name comes from the Sanskrit words for forest and protector, and was chosen as a tribute to the Assam Forest Department. Three of the four researchers behind the new study also worked on that one. According to the new paper, C. dimensis differs from it in both its genes and its body features.

According to the paper, this discovery takes the count of Cyrtodactylus species described from Assam to eight.

Umrangso is a town in Dima Hasao close to the Assam-Meghalaya border, about 112 km from Haflong, the district headquarters. The district is part of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot, and its hills, valleys, forests and changing altitudes offer many different habitats. The researchers said isolation and differences in habitat may explain why separate gecko species have evolved in the area, and called for more field surveys to record the district's reptiles.
